problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 17 public infrastructure projects to maximize the total community benefit score. The characteristics of each project are detailed as follows:
* Project A: benefit score is 0.165, implementation complexity is 0.147, funding range [0.078, 0.579]
* Project B: benefit score is 0.198, implementation complexity is 0.288, funding range [0.006, 0.557]
* Project C: benefit score is 0.061, implementation complexity is 0.251, funding range [0.080, 0.672]
* Project D: benefit score is 0.144, implementation complexity is 0.248, funding range [0.005, 0.361]
* Project E: benefit score is 0.192, implementation complexity is 0.161, funding range [0.061, 0.691]
* Project F: benefit score is 0.185, implementation complexity is 0.079, funding range [0.043, 0.705]
* Project G: benefit score is 0.055, implementation complexity is 0.031, funding range [0.010, 0.316]
* Project H: benefit score is 0.079, implementation complexity is 0.184, funding range [0.006, 0.610]
* Project I: benefit score is 0.031, implementation complexity is 0.137, funding range [0.005, 0.653]
* Project J: benefit score is 0.133, implementation complexity is 0.038, funding range [0.085, 0.365]
* Project K: benefit score is 0.025, implementation complexity is 0.139, funding range [0.040, 0.307]
* Project L: benefit score is 0.098, implementation complexity is 0.046, funding range [0.062, 0.728]
* Project M: benefit score is 0.024, implementation complexity is 0.293, funding range [0.041, 0.656]
* Project N: benefit score is 0.163, implementation complexity is 0.276, funding range [0.086, 0.804]
* Project O: benefit score is 0.188, implementation complexity is 0.119, funding range [0.079, 0.843]
* Project P: benefit score is 0.171, implementation complexity is 0.268, funding range [0.062, 0.376]
* Project Q: benefit score is 0.064, implementation complexity is 0.211, funding range [0.045, 0.605]

Each project must receive a budget allocation percentage that falls within its specified funding range, and the total allocation across all projects must sum to 100%. To ensure timely completion, the group of quick-delivery projects, represented by the subset L = {Q}, must collectively receive at least 5.4% of the total budget. Additionally, the overall implementation complexity of the portfolio must not exceed 0.174, and the total community benefit score must be no less than 0.104. Determine the optimal budget allocation percentages that maximize the total community benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
